findings.expected: Build receives one coherent, approved design package and can consume its hashed specification without inferring the implementation contract.
findings.observed: The r2 handoff points to the r2 manifest and approved phase verdict. The package-shape validator reports zero failures and one conditional summary slot; the manifest hashes the architecture and plan, and the implementation specification is part of the approved package.
findings.remediation: No separate summary artifact is needed for this intermediate boundary. Build management should reconcile the existing r1 implementation attempt against the r2 specification before treating any source as r2-complete.
findings.statement: A separate delivery summary is not required for this intermediate design-to-build handoff; the r2 handoff identifies the approved design manifest and build consumer, while the design package carries the architecture, plan, acceptance criteria, and implementation specification.
findings.verification: The boundary validator reports prior_reusable=true, changed_evidence=[], no failures, and no warnings. The delivery-shape validator reports zero failures, coherent r2 lineage, no skip record, and a clean blocked-phrase scan; only the optional summary slot is unchecked and is resolved out of scope for this handoff.
